# container-veths: a router in a container. Every interface is the inside
# end of a veth (no device link, iflink pointing into the host's namespace,
# 10 Gb/s), one per network zone, plus an ifb for SQM. There is no hardware
# port at all, so VirtualAuto reports the veths. The trap: eth0's iflink (22)
# equals the local ifb's ifindex (22); iflink is an index in the peer's
# namespace and must never be resolved locally. mac0 is a macvlan on lan0
# (iflink = a local ifindex, lower_lan0): stacked, not a port. vlan10 is a
# VLAN the host created and handed in (its parent is in the host's namespace,
# so there is no lower_* link): a virtual NIC like the veths. board.json is
# the host's and names the eth0 veth as LAN, which is ignored: board.json
# roles apply to hardware ports only. The WAN interfaces come from the caller
# (the collector's default routes).
#
# Format: see loadTree in ports_test.go.

-- etc/board.json --
{
	"model": {
		"id": "example,x86-host",
		"name": "Example x86 host"
	},
	"network": {
		"lan": {
			"device": "eth0",
			"protocol": "static"
		}
	}
}

-- sys/class/net/eth0/ --
type=1
ifindex=21
iflink=22
flags=0x1003
carrier=1
carrier_changes=2
operstate=up
speed=10000
duplex=full
address=02:00:00:00:04:21
mtu=1500
uevent=INTERFACE=eth0\nIFINDEX=21

-- sys/class/net/guest/ --
